**Change of the logic:** `StreamsAvailable` has been made a regular callback and moved to `QuicConnectionOptions` (thanks @rzikm for the suggestion). This is more aligned with how we handle callbacks/events in `SslStream`. After all, events are not a common occurrence in our stack. It also solves an issue with the correctness of the provided values in regards to thread safety. There's no chance of registering to the event in the middle of opening stream or processing `STREAMS_AVAILABLE` event. The callback is registered before the connection is created and the callback is always invoked as a reaction to a MsQuic event. The only thing that could happen is that invocations of the callback might swap order since we must offload the callback execution from MsQuic thread to the thread-pool. However, we are providing increments, so it doesn't matter that much as `a+b == b+a`.

issue_context.title: [HTTP/3] Implement connection scavenging
issue_context.body: We are not scavenging HTTP3 connections currently (i.e. based on idle timeout or lifetime). We need to implement this.
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/ncl See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
We are not scavenging HTTP3 connections currently (i.e. based on idle timeout or lifetime). We need to implement this.
Author: geoffkizer
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Net.Http`
Milestone: 6.0.0
Triage: Would manifest as memory leak

@geoffkizer What exactly is missing? I see we check the expiration and dispose and clean up the connection:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/f59a132bfe9ff797f9d192d67f07673a13b6b29e/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/HttpConnectionPool.cs#L812-L818
BTW, I think we should update the HTTP3 connection pooling logic in general to match the recent changes I made to HTTP11/2. As part of that, this should just fall out.
I changed the milestone to 7.0. We can't deliver production quality HTTP3 without this.

See also https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/60729, which has some proposals for how to change how connection scavenging works.

We should decide if we want to make any of those changes before we implement scavenging for HTTP3, to avoid wasted work.

review_comments: I was wondering why/how lifetime measurement is different from idle time measurement (meaning why it's not nullable) and that led to me wondering if it's now technically more correct to set `_creationTickCount` in `MarkConnectionAsEstablished` instead of `ctor`? >  Can someone set super small connection lifetime?

Yes, we do not check granularity, it can be as low as 1ns.


> if it's now technically more correct to set _creationTickCount in MarkConnectionAsEstablished

Not sure about this. What I can see is that we'd need to change the field to not `readonly` and make sure we don't touch it in between ctor and `MarkConnectionAsEstablished` anywhere. So, what exact issue do you see with the current state? Is it something that would not happen if we move the setting up of `_creationTickCount` to `MarkConnectionAsEstablished`?

Should it be `??=`? Or do I miss smth?
My view is that otherwise if the method is called twice, the first returned task will never be completed, as we'll lose the TaskCompletionSource object -- or is it impossible for it to be called concurrently?

I believe it's okay because there should only be 1 caller of `WaitForAvailableStreamsAsync` and at that point, the connection is not in the list of available connections on the pool.
It's probably worth a comment / assert though (we have the same logic on H2).
Added assert.
How is that different from `await Task.Yield();`?
It's effectively `await Task.Yield().ConfigureAwait(false)`
How is this better than having reference to parent QuicConection and calling an internal-only method directly?
See these comments: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/101531#discussion_r1612094496

Can we get MsQuic to expose increments instead of current counts?
(presumably, that's the data that they're reacting to that triggered these events in the first place?)

That'd let us drop the whole `DecrementAvailableStreamCount` dance

I like this idea. I can try that. It would also resolve the issue with the `_decrementAvailableStreamCount` callback. However, I'll not push on adding this to MsQuic, until we have the API approved, we might end up with MAX_STREAM_ID or different value being reported by the callback...

MsQuic change in https://github.com/microsoft/msquic/commit/d47f9c189a0070abe791e23daac9fd4f57c6f6cb

Makes sense. I'd like to see it happen but it's not worth blocking changes here.

Here too?
```suggestion
        public void StreamCapacityChangedCallback(QuicConnection connection, QuicStreamCapacityChangedArgs args)
```
Same reply as above.

We'll have to signal the `_availableStreamsWaiter` from here as well because `StreamsAvailableCallback` may not be called for a while if a bunch of streams got consumed by requests that were immediately canceled and released their streams.
Done.

In this case if `_streamCapacityCallback` is null, it won't allocate anything on the heap.
So I get that it's not worth any change :wink:
Nice catch :D

Should we also unset `_decrementStreamCapacity` here? 🤔
Or I guess it might be related to my question above re: `_decrementStreamCapacity` and `_startedTcs` alignment

It'll be already unset here. We set it when we call MsQuic `StreamStart` ==> we'll get `START_COMPLETE` 100% where we unset it. But the place I overlooked is when we get an error from `StreamStart`, I'll fix it.
Stupid question: why is `_decrementStreamCapacity(Type);` not aligned with `_startedTcs.TrySet...`?

It's aligned with MsQuic calculations. And MsQuic decrements right before signaling to us this event. So technically you can do to negative numbers, but all the streams bellow '0' will have to wait PEER_ACCEPT event.
EDIT: thinking about this more, what will happen when we have negative number here and we'll get STREAMS_AVAILABLE event??? Hmmm :thinking: Based on MsQuic, they report 0 if the capacity is not enough to get into positive numbers: https://github.com/microsoft/msquic/blob/f5bec530c8ef0824df7294f11d7b3516919899b1/src/core/stream_set.c#L482-L484

So I need to fix handling that event as well. And I'll add a test if I'll be able to simulate such situation.

So I added a test for this here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/101531/files#diff-82858b107709e3aeb48a21a06b9ac8a7898b6493db3637e97930b44ea4161a9fR234-R286
~And I had to change the behavior so that `_(b|un)idirectionalStreamCapacity` never goes into negatives. The changes are in this commit: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/101531/commits/2710d18adc116e2662baa2593508ee787ad6a9d1~

~What happens is that MsQuic will report zeros in STREAMS_AVAILABLE if the MAX_STREAMS update doesn't move the needle of the current capacity above 0 (i.e. it might have accepted some pending streams to be opened via PEER_ACCEPTED, but did not provide enough capacity to allow opening additional streams). To balance this out, we now ignore all the decrements that would lead bellow zero. Note that the decrements and STREAMS_AVAILABLE happen serially from a single thread. When we get down to zero, we might have some pending streams that are not peer accepted, when we get STREAMS_AVAILABLE with 0, it means we might have gotten some PEER_ACCEPTED, until we get STREAMS_AVAILABLE with positive value, which means that all pending streams were accepted and now we have some capacity to report.~

EDIT: **changed my mind about this slightly. Allowing it to go into negatives and report every increment is more in line with future behavior of https://github.com/microsoft/msquic/commit/b4b6fc5a181e8522102421785a9e8bd19fbaf081, so I'll try to make this behave the same as how would it behave with the change in MsQuic.**

Feel free to think about this more and poke holes into my logic.

Lastly, I hope to change this and offload the counting fully into MsQuic. But as I mentioned above, I don't want to hold this waiting on the next MsQuic release.

But I think we can fix this, from what I see in the source code, we can reliably calculate
- total number of created streams (by counting successful STREAM_STARTED events)
- total number of started streams (PeerAccepted in STREAM_STARTED or PEER_ACCEPTED events)

in addition to current counts, we maintain the above counts also for the moment when the last STREAMS_AVAILABLE was received. Since PEER_STARTED will be fired before STREAMS_AVAILABLE, by keeping the delta we can detect exactly how much of the "new" capacity was consumed by pending streams, so we can reliably calculate the total increment received over the wire.

If my explanation was not clear enough, I can have a go at implementing this myself.
That's what I'm working on right now. It's the bold edit in my comment above. Basically, counting the number of PEER_ACCEPTED towards the increments.

UPDATE: I added your test and also added another test that cancels the pending `OpenOutboundStream`. Which led me to discover that PEER_ACCEPTED counting is not enough. The canceled streams during open do not receive PEER_ACCEPTED as they get SHUTDOWN with IMMEDIATE flag. So to keep the logic simple, I just wait for the capacity to get above 0 and then I report the difference cumulatively.
Example with capacity 3:
- callback with initial capacity 3
- open 3 streams ==> OK
- try to open another 3 ==> pending
- close first 3 ==> no callback yet, but pending 3 streams get accepted
- close 1 stream ==> callback reports 4
- close remaining 2 streams ==> 2x callback with 1
- together callback called with the sum of 6

This will lead to the same callbacks if you cancel the pending streams in step 3 or not.

Note that when we move the increments counting into MsQuic, we will report the increments in step 4 (based on every MAX_STREAMS). 

Also the current logic with held back callback could be improved with the PEER_ACCEPTED, but we'd still need the logic for canceled streams and I feel like the complicated code is not worth it as we:
1. do not go into negatives with multiple connections (so we don't use this)
2. we plan to switch to MsQuic increment counting (which will slightly alter the behavior anyway)

What's unchanged is that we'll cumulatively (eventually) report the same sum.
